title: Deadlock Arena
subtitle: Interactive simulation of lock contention and deadlock between transactions
simulationBadgeNote: Local simulation of two contending transaction sessions. Runs entirely inside the browser without network egress.

scenarios.label: Scenario
scenarios.deadlock_reverse_order: Deadlock from updates in reverse order

about.deadlock_reverse_order: Two sessions update two rows in opposite order, creating a mutual wait-for cycle.
about.lost_update: Two sessions read the same value and overwrite it; one update vanishes.
about.write_skew: Two transactions read shared data but update separate rows, violating an overall business rule.
about.double_booking: Two sessions both see an empty slot and simultaneously book it.
about.non_repeatable_read: One session reads the same row twice and observes different values because another session committed in between.

view.deadlockDetail: Detected circular wait-for cycle (SQLSTATE 40P01). Transaction A was aborted to resolve deadlock.
view.conflictDetail: Conflict occurred when two transactions operated on competing data.

step0.title: Data initialization
step0.description: Table accounts is created with two rows id=1 (100) and id=2 (100).

step1.title: Start 2 transactions
step1.description: Transaction A and Transaction B both start with READ COMMITTED isolation level.

step2.title: Update accounts in order
step2.description: Transaction A updates and locks account 1. Transaction B updates and locks account 2.

step3.title: Circular wait-for conflict
step3.description: Transaction A requests lock on account 2 (held by B). Transaction B requests lock on account 1 (held by A) -> Deadlock cycle appears!

step4.title: Lock release and completion
step4.description: PostgreSQL engine aborts Transaction A with error 40P01 (deadlock detected). Transaction B resumes and completes COMMIT.

step0.title: Data initialization
step0.description: Table accounts is created with row id=1 (100).

step1.title: Start 2 transactions
step1.description: Transaction A and Transaction B both start with READ COMMITTED.

step3.title: Overwrite balance
step3.description: Transaction A updates balance = 110. Transaction B updates balance = 120.

step4.title: Lost update occurs
step4.description: Transaction B commits last and completely overwrites Transaction A's update.

step0.title: Data initialization
step0.description: Table doctors has 2 doctors on call (id=1, id=2 on_call = true).

step1.title: Start 2 transactions
step1.description: Transaction A and Transaction B start with REPEATABLE READ.

step2.title: Check on-call count
step2.description: Both transactions check and see count = 2 (sufficient doctors to request leave).

step3.title: Simultaneous leave request
step3.description: Transaction A sets doctor 1 off call. Transaction B sets doctor 2 off call.

step4.title: Constraint broken (Write Skew)
step4.description: Both transactions commit successfully, but zero doctors remain on call (count = 0).

step0.title: Data initialization
step0.description: Bookings and rooms setup, slot 1 is vacant.

step1.title: Start 2 transactions
step1.description: Transaction A and B both start with READ COMMITTED.

step2.title: Check room vacancy
step2.description: Both transactions check and observe slot 1 is currently vacant.

step3.title: Concurrent reservation
step3.description: Transaction A and B both dispatch INSERT queries to claim slot 1.

step4.title: Duplicate reservation (Double Booking)
step4.description: Both transactions commit, resulting in duplicate reservations for the same slot.

step0.title: Data initialization
step0.description: Table accounts is created with row id=1 (100).

step1.title: Start 2 transactions
step1.description: Transaction A and B both start with READ COMMITTED.

step2.title: First read and update
step2.description: Transaction A reads balance = 100. Transaction B updates balance = 200 and commits.

step3.title: Second read in same transaction
step3.description: Transaction A reads row id=1 again and sees balance = 200 instead of 100.

step4.title: Transaction completion
step4.description: Transaction A commits with inconsistent read values.
